page: Amazon Web Services g7e.12xlarge is an accelerated computing instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8559C processor running at 2.4 GHz, supplying 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs with 320 MB of L3 cache, complemented by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel AMX. System memory comprises 512 GB of high-frequency 6 GHz DDR5 RAM, delivering 10.67 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by two bundled NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs offering a combined 192 GB of VRAM. High-speed local persistence includes a bundled 3800 GB NVMe SSD, paired with a baseline network bandwidth of 400 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong graphics and machine learning performance, driven by the Blackwell GPU subsystem. Large language model inference benchmarks place the instance in the top 10% tier, producing prompt processing rates of 7164.24 tokens per second on 7B models and 1264.93 tokens per second on 70B models. Text generation achieves 175.65 tokens per second on 7B parameters and 28.25 tokens per second on 70B parameters. Geekbench results echo this acceleration, registering top-tier results in image processing alongside strong marks in ray tracing and single-core compute. In memory and disk throughput, Redis SET operations reached 69.67 million operations per second, supported by un-cached read bandwidth measuring 225.52 GB per second.

The instance balances dedicated acceleration with robust peripheral subsystems, though raw CPU-bound stress-ng multi-core and single-core test scores sit within the middle 50% category. In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the high concentration of 192 GB VRAM, coupled with 3800 GB of fast local NVMe storage and 400 Gbps networking, delivers significant resource density for jobs that would otherwise require multiple smaller accelerated nodes. This configuration minimizes inter-node communication bottlenecks during large-scale tasks.

Amazon Web Services g7e.12xlarge is tailored for heavy GPU-centric tasks, including mid-to-large-scale generative AI and LLM inference, real-time ray tracing, high-end 3D graphics rendering, and video processing pipelines. The substantial memory footprint and high I/O throughput also make it effective for low-latency distributed caching, in-memory databases, and high-throughput analytical ETL workflows.

It is equipped with 512 GB of 6 GHz DDR5 memory, dual NVIDIA Blackwell RTX PRO 6000 GPUs totaling 192 GB of VRAM, 3800 GB of bundled NVMe SSD storage, and a 400 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark evaluations highlight top-decile performance in LLM inference, reaching 7164.24 prompt tokens per second on 7B models, along with superior image processing and ray tracing scores. This instance is suited for large-scale AI inference, ray tracing, visual computing, and data-intensive analytical pipelines.
